correctness.rationale: A full orthonormal character decomposition produces 2×2 nontrivial blocks of squared Gauss modulus q and a real 3×3 trivial block. The characteristic polynomials in each of three exhaustive nonsingular geometries yield every squared singular value. Algebraic comparison proves the sharp κ values, and finite-field projective isotropy proves optimizer counts for all q, separately including q=2. Direct full-matrix computations agree on 589 two-line pairs over eleven fields. No extrapolation is used for the theorem.

value.rationale: A complete optimal-design classification for a natural finite-field union-of-lines sampling system gives sharp least singular values, exact counts of stable samplers, and an unbounded improvement factor √q/φ when isotropic lines exist. This quantifies noise robustness not supplied by binary invertibility, and is a motivated all-prime-power design invariant rather than arbitrary finite enumeration.
